metadata.description: Run 8: Powered Follow-Up - Triple Conjunction {C,D,E} (seed 601): 5 cells, 200 episodes
metadata.switch_mechanism: The rule switches after the 3rd time the detector activates (turns on). The env_info.successful_activations field counts total activations; env_info.rule_switched indicates whether the switch occurred.
key_methodology_notes: Decomposition uses env_info.rule_switched as authoritative for whether the rule switched during the episode.
Pre-switch episodes (rule_switched=False) have true_objects=[A,B]. Post-switch episodes (rule_switched=True) have true_objects=[C,D,E].
DB mechanism operates through: (1) trigger token injection into conversation as system messages about rule changes, (2) enabling MODERATOR_DETECTION CG state.
All 75 DB episodes (C+E) have trigger_tokens > 0. The step-level db_notifications array is always empty; DB operates via conversation injection.
Post-switch accuracy is the primary comparison metric, as pre-switch episodes are trivial 'freebies'.

section_2_activation_count_decomposition.explanation: Episodes are split by whether the hidden moderator rule switch occurred (env_info.rule_switched). Pre-switch episodes have true rule {A,B} and are trivial 'freebies' where guessing the initial rule is correct. Post-switch episodes have true rule {C,D,E} and require detecting the rule change.

pre_switch_freebie.note: Rule never switched (< 3 activations). True rule = {A,B}. Guessing {A,B} is correct.

post_switch_reasoning.note: Rule switched (>= 3 activations). True rule = {C,D,E}. Agent must detect the change and identify new blickets.

section_2_activation_count_decomposition.key_finding: Pre-switch freebies are unevenly distributed across cells. base_llm (Cell A) has 13/50 (26%) pre-switch episodes because it answers quickly before triggering 3 activations. CG agents (B: 3/50, C: 4/50) take more steps and almost always trigger the rule switch. This makes raw accuracy misleading: A's 70% is inflated by freebies while B's 68% understates its post-switch reasoning. Post-switch accuracy -- A: 59.5%, B: 66.0%, C: 89.1% -- is the proper comparison metric.

section_3_error_classification.explanation: Every wrong episode is classified. Main categories: post_switch_wrong_objects (correct rule type, wrong objects), post_switch_wrong_type (wrong rule type), timeout (max steps without answer), no_answer (didn't submit). Sub-categories for wrong objects: stuck_on_pre_switch_rule_AB, guessed_all_five_ABCDE, superset_of_true, subset_of_true.
key_findings: The dominant error is post_switch_wrong_objects (48/51 errors = 94.1%). Agents almost always identify conjunctive rule type correctly but fail on objects.
Two main failure modes: stuck_on_pre_switch_rule_AB (33/48 = 68.8% of wrong-object errors) and guessed_all_five_ABCDE (14/48 = 29.2%).
Cell B (cg_only) has the highest stuck-on-AB rate among its post-switch errors: 14/15 (93.3%). CG reinforces initial hypotheses.
Cell A (base_llm) shows a more balanced split: 7 stuck on {A,B} and 8 guessed all five. base_llm explores more but over-includes.
Cell C (full_cg_db) has only 5 total errors, of which 3 are stuck-on-AB and 1 is all-five. DB dramatically reduces all error types.
Only 1 timeout (Cell B), 1 wrong rule type (Cell E), and 1 pre-switch wrong (Cell E, parse failure at 9 steps).

section_4_db_mechanism_analysis.explanation: Dynamic Behavior (DB) analysis for cells C and E (full_cg_db agents). DB injects trigger tokens as system messages about rule changes and enables MODERATOR_DETECTION CG state for systematic investigation.

mechanism_details.trigger_tokens: Always >0 for DB agents. Represents tokens injected into the conversation by the DB system.
mechanism_details.system_message: DB injects '[SYSTEM] The causal rule appears to have changed. A new MODERATOR_DETECTION state is available to investigate rule shifts.'
mechanism_details.moderator_detection_state: CG state enabling systematic rule-change investigation, including re-testing objects under new regime.
mechanism_details.step_level_db_notifications: Always empty arrays in traces. DB operates through conversation injection, not discrete step notifications.

key_findings: All 75 DB episodes have trigger_tokens > 0 -- the DB system always injects content.
DB injects system messages about rule changes. Among post-switch episodes, Cell C receives the message in 44/46 (95.7%) cases; Cell E in 20/24 (83.3%).
CRITICAL FINDING: System message reception strongly correlates with success. Cell C: 93.2% accuracy with message vs 0.0% without (n=2). Cell E: 90.0% with message vs 0.0% without (n=4).
MODERATOR_DETECTION state is triggered in 22/46 (47.8%) of Cell C post-switch episodes and 7/24 (29.2%) of Cell E.
Cell C: MD-triggered post-switch accuracy (90.9%) vs non-MD (87.5%) -- modest difference, suggesting the system message alone is highly effective.
Cell E: MD-triggered post-switch accuracy (85.7%) vs non-MD (70.6%) -- larger difference, suggesting MD state is more valuable under step pressure.
First MODERATOR_DETECTION step: Cell C mean=30.4 (median=29.0), Cell E mean=28.7 (median=31.0).

findings.conclusion: base_llm never uses more than 48 steps. The 25 extra steps in Cell A provide no meaningful benefit. Accuracy is virtually identical (70.0% vs 68.0%), well within sampling noise for N=25/50.

full_cg_db_75_vs_50.description: Cell C (full_cg_db, 75 steps) vs Cell E (full_cg_db, 50 steps)

findings.pct_over_50_in_C: 56.0% of Cell C episodes use >50 steps
findings.conclusion: full_cg_db is step-hungry: 56.0% of Cell C episodes exceed 50 steps. When capped at 50 (Cell E), raw accuracy drops from 90.0% to 72.0%. The extra runway is critical for the systematic verification approach.

section_7_three_way_comparison.description: A (base_llm, 75 steps) vs B (cg_only, 75 steps) vs C (full_cg_db, 75 steps). All at same max_steps for controlled comparison.

primary_question.question: Does full_cg_db's advantage come from CG structure or from DB specifically?
primary_question.answer: DB is the primary driver (78% of the advantage), but CG also contributes meaningfully (22%). Post-switch accuracy -- the true measure after removing freebie pre-switch episodes -- shows: A (base_llm) = 59.5%, B (cg_only) = 66.0%, C (full_cg_db) = 89.1%. CG alone provides a +6.5pp boost, and adding DB provides a further +23.1pp boost.
primary_question.critical_note_on_raw_accuracy: Raw accuracy is MISLEADING for this comparison because Cell A has 13/50 (26%) pre-switch freebie episodes while B and C have only 3-4/50 (6-8%). base_llm answers quickly and sometimes answers before triggering the 3rd activation (rule never switches, true rule remains {A,B}). This inflates A's raw accuracy. Post-switch accuracy is the proper comparison metric.

pre_switch_freebie_rates.A: 13/50 (26.0%) - base_llm answers quickly, often before rule switch
pre_switch_freebie_rates.B: 3/50 (6.0%) - CG agents take more steps, almost always trigger switch
pre_switch_freebie_rates.C: 4/50 (8.0%) - CG agents take more steps, almost always trigger switch

error_pattern_analysis.interpretation: CG agents (B, C) are MORE likely to get stuck on {A,B} when they fail, suggesting CG reinforces initial hypotheses. However, B fails less often overall in post-switch episodes than A does.

interpretation.raw_accuracy_is_misleading: Cell A's raw 70% is inflated by 13 pre-switch freebie episodes (26% of total). Cell B's raw 68% understates its true post-switch reasoning ability. Post-switch accuracy is the correct metric.
interpretation.cg_alone_helps_modestly: Cell B post-switch accuracy (66.0%) exceeds Cell A (59.5%) by 6.5pp. CG structure provides modest benefit for detecting rule changes, likely through its systematic state-based exploration (INITIAL_EXPLORATION -> COMBINATION_TESTING -> HYPOTHESIS_EVALUATION -> VERIFICATION).
interpretation.db_provides_dramatic_boost: Cell C post-switch accuracy (89.1%) exceeds Cell B (66.0%) by 23.1pp. DB's rule-change notification system and MODERATOR_DETECTION state are the dominant mechanism driving accuracy.
interpretation.cg_reinforces_hypotheses_on_failure: When CG agents DO fail, they are much more likely to be stuck on the pre-switch rule {A,B}: B has 14/16 (87.5%) stuck-on-AB errors vs A's 7/15 (46.7%). CG creates more rigid beliefs that, without DB's rule-change alert, resist revision.
interpretation.attribution_summary: Of the 29.6pp post-switch accuracy gap between A and C: CG contributes ~22% (6.5pp) and DB contributes ~78% (23.1pp).
interpretation.cost_efficiency: A: $0.42/correct, B: $1.14/correct, C: $1.37/correct. C's cost premium per correct answer is 3.3x relative to A, but delivers 29.6pp higher post-switch accuracy.
